comments.author: notnmeyer
comments.body: change the label to something that makes sense on its own, "ai-code-review-single-run" or something

items.why: The PR title and body promise a `hankles (limited edition)` label ("tag" in the title), but the last commit renamed it to `one-shot-ai-review`, which is the only name the workflow matches. The body is the text that survives the squash merge, so it now names a label that does nothing.

The concurrency group is set at the workflow level with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so adding any unrelated label during a one-shot review starts a skipped run that still cancels the review. The removal step then never runs and the label stays on the PR, so the next push runs a review again. That breaks the body's claim that the review runs once and the label comes off when it is done.

comments.author: john-hankles
comments.body:
The `|| echo "Label already removed."` fallback hides every failure, not only the 404 case. The GitHub App token needs `issues: write` to delete a label from a pull request. If the installation does not have it, the API call returns 403, the step still passes, and the label stays on the pull request. The one-shot label then becomes permanent, and each later push starts a new review. Please let the step fail on anything that is not a 404.

```suggestion
        run: |
          if ! gh api -X DELETE "repos/${GH_REPO}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/labels/hankles%20%28limited%20edition%29" --silent 2> label-error.log; then
            grep -q "HTTP 404" label-error.log || { cat label-error.log; exit 1; }
          fi
```

evidence.why: `|| echo` does swallow every non-zero exit, including 403s and 5xx errors, so the general point is real and the suggested 404-only fallback is a small fix.

The same app token already posts inline review comments and resolves threads, so the installation has `pull_requests: write`. As far as I know, GitHub's label endpoints accept that permission or `issues: write`, so the 403 scenario the comment names is unlikely. I could not confirm the app's installed permissions from the repo.
If the delete did fail silently, the next push would start another review, so the failure shows up on its own. It does not linger unseen.
The cache save uses `!cancelled()`, so letting the delete step fail, as the suggestion does, would not lose the saved session. Adopting it costs little.

note.draftReply: Keeping this as-is: the app token already holds pull_requests: write (it posts the review comments), and that permission covers label deletes. If a delete ever did fail, the next push would run a second review, which is loud enough on its own.
